editorial_note: Canto 11 data remains under full source and translation review. The Sanskrit and English records are draft material tied to the pinned source; phrase coverage and all lexical choices still require chapter-by-chapter verification.

entries.sanskrit: प्रीतिम् आविष्करोति---सम्यग् इति त्रिभिः । पृच्छसे पृच्छसि । विश्व-भावनान् सर्व-शोधकान् ॥११॥
entries.literal_english: He expresses his pleasure in the three verses beginning 'well.' 'You inquire' means 'you ask'; 'promoting the world's welfare' means 'purifying everyone.'

entries.sanskrit: आदृत आस्तिक्येन गृहीतः । अनुमोदितः परैः क्रियमाणः संस्तुतः । सद्-धर्मो भागवतो धर्मः । देव ! हे वसुदेव ! इत्य् अर्थः । यद् वा, देवेभ्यो विश्वस्मै च द्रुह्यन्ति ये, तान् अपि ॥१२॥
word_for_word: the dharma of the Lord's devotees
entries.literal_english: 'Honored' means accepted with faith. 'Approved' means praised when others carry it out. 'True dharma' is bhāgavata-dharma. One reading takes 'deva' as the address 'O Vasudeva!' Alternatively, the expression refers even to those who are hostile to the gods and to the world.
entries.note: Śrīdhara gives two interpretations of the verse's 'deva-viśva-druhaḥ'; neither is silently selected as the sole meaning.

entries.sanskrit: किं च, त्वया महान् उपकारः कृत इत्य् आह---त्वयेति । पुण्ये श्रवण-कीर्तने यस्य सः ॥१३॥
word_for_word: he whose [hearing and praise] are such
entries.literal_english: Moreover, he says 'by you' to indicate that you have done a great favor: [Nārāyaṇa] is the one whose hearing and praise are meritorious.
entries.note: The source's verse marker for 11.2.13 has malformed Markdown; this separate checkpoint retains the clearly labelled Śrīdhara text.

word_for_word: also in the determination of devotion to the Lord
entries.literal_english: 'Here too' means also in determining the dharma of the Lord. 'Of Videha' means of Janaka.

entries.sanskrit: आर्षभाणाम् उत्पत्तिं सान्वयां विविच्य कथयति---प्रियव्रत इति सप्तभिः ॥१५॥
entries.literal_english: He recounts the origin of the descendants of Ṛṣabha, distinguishing them and tracing their lineage in seven verses beginning 'Priyavrata.'

entries.sanskrit: मोक्ष-धर्म-विवक्षया मोक्ष-धर्माणां प्रवर्तनेच्छया अवतीर्णं वासुदेवांशम् आह---तस्य च वेद-पारगं सुत-शतम् आसीत् ॥१६॥
word_for_word: with the intention of teaching the dharma of liberation
from the desire to promulgate the practices leading to liberation
entries.literal_english: 'With the intention of teaching the dharma of liberation' means descending from a desire to promulgate the practices of liberation. He calls [Ṛṣabha] a portion of Vāsudeva; that figure had a hundred sons versed in the Veda.

entries.sanskrit: तेषाम् ऋषभ-सुतानां मध्ये नव-योगीश्वराणां चरितं वक्तुम् इतरेषां चरितं ततो विविच्याह---तेषाम् इति । एतद् अजनाभं नाम वर्षं यस्य नाम्ना भारतम् इत्य् अद्भुतं विख्यातम् आसीत् । एतेन तस्य धर्मातिरेको निरूपितः ॥१७॥
word_for_word: in order to recount the story of the nine Yogīśvaras
he distinguishes from that and says
entries.literal_english: To tell the story of the nine Yogīśvaras among Ṛṣabha's sons, he first distinguishes the accounts of the other sons, beginning 'of them.' This land, once called Ajanābha, became remarkably famous as Bhārata through [Bharata's] name. This indicates his exceptional commitment to dharma.

entries.sanskrit: इमां पृथ्वीम् । गृहान् निर्गतः । हरिम् उपासीनः सेवमानः सन् ॥१८॥
entries.literal_english: 'This' means the earth. 'Having departed' means having left home. 'Worshipping Hari' means serving him.

entries.sanskrit: नव सुताः नव-द्वीप-पतयो नवानां ब्रह्मावर्तादि-भू-खण्डानां पतयः । अस्य भारतस्य वर्षस्य । एकाशीतिः सुताः कर्म-मार्ग-प्रवर्तका ब्राह्मणा अभूवन् ॥१८॥
word_for_word: promoters of the path of ritual action
entries.literal_english: Nine sons became rulers of nine divisions of this Bhārata region, beginning with Brahmāvarta. The other eighty-one sons became brahmins who advanced the path of ritual action.
entries.note: The pinned commentary to verse 19 itself ends with ॥१८॥. That inconsistent verse number is retained as a source reading, not silently corrected.

entries.sanskrit: अर्थ-शंसिनः परमार्थ-निरूपकाः । श्रमणाः श्रमवन्तः, आत्माभ्यासे कृत-श्रमा इत्य् अर्थः । वात-वसना दिग्-अम्बराः । आत्म-विद्यायां विशारदा निष्णाताः ॥२०-२१॥
word_for_word: those who describe the true aim
entries.literal_english: 'Those who explain the aim' means expositors of the highest truth. 'Ascetics' means people who have exerted themselves in the practice of self-knowledge. 'Clothed in the wind' means clothed only in the directions. 'Adept in knowledge of the self' means thoroughly proficient.
entries.note: The source places a single commentary under the combined heading 11.2.20–21; it has not been split into fictitious independent verse glosses.

scope: Complete source-bound Śrīdhara commentary for Canto 11 Chapter 2, verses 11.2.11–11.2.21.
